messages:
kyle: Nightly GPU CI is red on job #17845 (nightly-gpu-ubuntu-2204) — kernel oops in nvidia module, can't boot container. Dump below, marking for bisect?

ci-bot: Job 17845 failed — tests/executor/gpu_smoke.py::test_large_allreduce — see logs: https://ci.internal/17845 :x:

maria: Ugh. Any driver/cuda mismatch in the logs? sometimes the new ubuntu kernel + driver combo trips DKMS.

kyle: Quick paste from the runner dmesg (sanitized):

```
[  423.512345] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00: GPU-1234abcd-5678
[  423.512347] NVRM: Kernel module is from the wrong version of the NVIDIA driver
[  423.512348] NVRM: Found no NVIDIA GPU driver on your system.
[  423.512999] NVRM: Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch
[  424.000001] kauditd_printk_skb: 23 callbacks suppressed
[  424.100200] NVRM: GPU Xid: 31: PID=4321:  Xid (PCIe) 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
```

samir: Classic driver/library mismatch. Which container image are we using? CUDA toolchain likely 12.2 in the image while host has 535.86 driver or vice versa.

kyle: Runner image: quay.redwood/ci/gpu-ubuntu-2204:cuda-12.2-runtime (we updated base last week). Host driver reported by runner before crash: 540.2.

maria: That explains it — CUDA 12.2 is usually paired with 525/535 drivers, 540 can be newer and sometimes ABI changes cause NVML init failures. Could be the kernel module built for 540 isn't compatible with the runtime.

jen: Can we repro locally? If someone can spin the same host driver + image combo we could confirm. Also please attach full /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and container stdout.

kyle: Attached short logs in the job artifacts (link above). I reproduced quickly with a VM that had driver 540 and the container — got the same Xid 79.

noah: Temporary mitigation: requeue the job to a runner pinned to driver 535 or fallback to older host image. Ops added a label runner:driver=535 on a few pools.

opsbot: Rerun requested by noah on job 17845 -> new job 17846 queued on runner gpu-rt-17 (driver=535). :gear:

ci-bot: Job 17846 started.

kyle: Rerun 17846 passed on that runner (:thumbsup:), but another nightly on kernel edge (gpu-rt-22 with driver 540) still fails intermittently. I think we have a compatibility regression exposed by a recent kernel upgrade.

maria: Can we bisect the infra change? last infra change that touched runners was: bump-kernel-5.19->6.1 (commit a1b2c3d) and driver rollback change (commit f4e5f6). Which commit range covers this?

samir: I can take a git-bisect on the runner-config repo. Need a 'good' commit (where nightly passed) and 'bad' (current failing). kyle, can you paste the earliest failing job timestamp and a recent good job?

kyle: Good: job 1768001200 (branch main) passed on 2026-05-20. Bad: first failure seen job 1768990001 on 2026-12-01. Suspect the infra rollouts happened between those.

samir: Great — I'll start bisect tomorrow morning. Steps I'll run:
```
git clone git@repo:infra/runner-config.git
git bisect start
git bisect bad <bad-sha>
git bisect good <good-sha>
# then run ansible deploy in a test env and rerun the gpu smoke job
```
If someone can point me to an easy way to rerun just the smoke test against a specific runner image, that'd help.

jen: For quicker triage, can we also try a stress-run of GPU memory allocations inside the container to see if Xid 79 is actually a PCIe fault or OOM? small script:
```
python -c "import torch; a=[]
for i in range(40):
  a.append(torch.empty(1024,1024,device='cuda'))"
```
If it crashes consistently, likely OOM/driver bug.

noah: FYI I added a retry policy in CI to reschedule on driver=535 for the immediate nightly windows. Not ideal long-term but buys time.

maria: Once samir narrows commit, we should open an eng-runtime ticket and cc infra + eng-sre. Also add a note in the release channel so we don't uplift problematic kernel/driver combos.

kyle: Thanks all. Samir — ping me when you start the bisect and I'll keep the failed jobs and artifacts preserved.

samir: Will do. If bisect points to kernel change, I'll try reproducing locally with the matching kernel headers and see if DKMS rebuild is introducing the mismatch. If it's a driver packaging bug, we should pin driver to 535 in the runners until driver vendor fixes ABI. :thinking:

jen: thumbs up. Also adding a short checklist in the job template for GPU jobs: log nvml, run dmesg dump, and avoid rolling host drivers during heavy CI windows.

kyle: Updated ticket in #infra-ops with links to artifacts and the sample dmesg. Leaving job artifacts preserved. Thanks everyone. :pray:
